en.B: These are the people of the province who came up out of the captivity of the exiles whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away to Babylon. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to {{gender:their|his}} own town,
en.R: This is a list of the people of the province of Judah who came back from exile. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken them away as prisoners to Babylon. Now they returned to Jerusalem and the rest of Judah. Each family went back to its own town.

es.L: Y estos [son] los hijos de la provincia que subieron del cautiverio del destierro, a quienes Nabucodonosor rey de Babilonia había llevado al destierro a Babilonia, y volvieron a Jerusalén y a Judá, cada uno a su ciudad,
es.B: Estos son los de la provincia que subieron del cautiverio de los desterrados, a quienes Nabucodonosor rey de Babilonia había deportado a Babilonia. Volvieron a Jerusalén y a Judá, cada uno a su propia ciudad,
es.R: Esta es la lista de la gente de la provincia de Judá que regresó del destierro. Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia, se los había llevado presos a Babilonia. Ahora volvieron a Jerusalén y al resto de Judá. Cada familia regresó a su propia ciudad.

fr.L: Et voici les fils de la province qui montèrent de la captivité de l’exil, que Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, avait déportés à Babylone, et ils revinrent à Jérusalem et en Juda, chacun dans sa ville,
fr.B: Voici les gens de la province qui remontèrent de la captivité des exilés que Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, avait déportés à Babylone. Ils revinrent à Jérusalem et en Juda, chacun dans sa ville,
fr.R: Voici la liste des gens de la province de Juda qui sont revenus de l’exil. Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, les avait emmenés comme prisonniers à Babylone. Ils sont alors revenus à Jérusalem et dans le reste de Juda. Chaque famille est retournée dans sa propre ville.

sw.L: Na hawa [ndio] wana wa jimbo waliopanda kutoka katika utumwa wa uhamisho, ambao Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli alikuwa amewahamishia Babeli, nao wakarudi Yerusalemu na Yuda, kila mmoja kwenye mji wake,

decisions.choice: Zerubbabel and Jeshua: the governor of David's line and the high priest
decisions.reason: Zerubbabel was a grandson of King Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3:17-19) and became governor of Judah (Haggai 1:1). Jeshua son of Jozadak was the high priest (Ezra 3:2); Haggai and Zechariah call him Joshua (Haggai 1:1; Zechariah 3:1). They lead the rebuilding in chapters 3-6.

decisions.choice: Nehemiah and Mordecai: other men of the same names
decisions.reason: These are leaders of the first return. They are not Nehemiah the governor, who came about ninety years later (Nehemiah 2:1), nor Esther's cousin Mordecai, who lived in Susa (Esther 2:5).

decisions.choice: eleven names here, twelve in Nehemiah 7:7
decisions.reason: Nehemiah 7:7 has twelve leaders: it adds Nahamani and has Azariah for Seraiah, Raamiah for Reelaiah, Mispereth for Mispar and Nehum for Rehum. Twelve leaders may stand for the twelve tribes of Israel, as the twelve offerings do in Ezra 6:17 and 8:35.

decisions.choice: "Zorobabel", "Jesúa", "Nehemías", "Mardoqueo"
decisions.reason: Names in the forms already published (Zorobabel, 1 Chronicles 3:19; Jesúa, 2 Chronicles 31:15) or long usual in Spanish; the rest of the list is spelled from the Hebrew in the same way.

decisions.choice: "Zerubabeli", "Yeshua"; the other leaders in the usual Swahili forms ("Nehemia", "Mordekai")
decisions.reason: "Yeshua" is the terms-note form for the high priest, kept apart from Joshua son of Nun ("Yoshua"); "Zerubabeli" as 1 Chronicles 3:19.

decisions.choice: "Zorobabel", "Yeshoua", "Néhémie", "Mardochée"
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Zerubbabel is "Zorobabel" (Matthew 1:12) and Jeshua "Yeshoua", as the terms note; Nehemiah and Mordecai take their familiar French forms even though they are other men. The names of the lists that French has published elsewhere keep that form ("Seraya", "Baana", "Shephatia", "Rama", "Guéba", "Pashhour"); the others are spelled from the Hebrew in the same way ("sh", "ou", "ts", "q" for qof, "ï" for a final -ai).

decisions.choice: Xô-rô-ba-bên, Giê-sua, Nê-hê-mi, Mạc-đô-chê
decisions.reason: Zerubbabel keeps the form of Matthew 1:12 and Jeshua that of 2 Chronicles 31:15. Nehemiah and Mordecai are other men than the governor and Esther's cousin (m2), but take the same familiar forms, as the English does. The other names are spelled from the Hebrew in the usual Vietnamese way.

decisions.choice: the sons of Parosh: the members of the family descended from Parosh
decisions.reason: "Sons of" in this list means the members of a family or clan named after its ancestor, as "the sons of Israel" means the Israelites. The numbers count the people of each family who came back. Verses 3-20 are mostly family names; from verse 21 most entries are towns.

decisions.choice: the descendants of (Balanced, Readable); the sons of (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "descendants", which is what the phrase means and includes women; Literal keeps "sons".

decisions.choice: "[los] hijos de" (L); "los descendientes de" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for "sons of X" in the lists (terms note), as the English: Literal keeps "hijos", Balanced and Readable say "descendientes", which takes in women. Numbers of four digits and more are written with a space (2 172).

decisions.choice: "wana wa" (L); "wazao wa" (B, R) in the lists
decisions.reason: As the English: "wazao" says what the phrase means and includes women; Literal keeps "wana". Numbers above ninety-nine are in figures with a comma, as the Chronicles drafts.

decisions.choice: các con của (Literal); con cháu (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Sons of" before a family name means the clan descended from that ancestor (m1). Literal keeps "các con của", which still says "sons, children"; Balanced and Readable say "con cháu", which includes women. Numbers above ninety-nine are in figures through the list, with a dot for thousands, as in 1 Chronicles 9.

decisions.choice: the Nethinim: the temple servants, "those given" to the temple
decisions.reason: The word means "the given ones". They were people given to the temple to help the Levites in its work; Ezra 8:20 says David and his officials gave them for the service of the Levites. They may go back to foreigners put to work at the sanctuary, like the Gibeonites who became "cutters of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God" (Joshua 9:23, 27); some names in this list, such as Meunim and Nephusim (verse 50), look foreign. After the return they belonged fully to the community (Nehemiah 10:29).

decisions.choice: Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan, Immer: places in Babylonia
decisions.reason: These are settlements where the exiles lived, like Tel-abib by the Chebar canal (Ezekiel 3:15). "Tel" means a mound, the ruin of an old town, on which a new village could be built. Nehemiah 7:61 has Addon for Addan.

decisions.choice: Barzillai the Gileadite: the man who helped David

decisions.choice: was called by their name: took the name of his wife's family
decisions.reason: "Their" refers to Barzillai's daughters, that is, to his family. Taking the wife's family name may have been for the sake of an inheritance (compare Numbers 36:1-12).

decisions.choice: Readable adds "could not prove their families either"
decisions.reason: The next verse shows that these priests were in the same position as the families of verses 59-60; Readable says so at the start.

decisions.choice: "Cos", "Barzilai el galaadita"
decisions.reason: Hakkoz as the published Spanish of 1 Chronicles 24:10 has it ("Cos", without the article the name carries in Hebrew); Barzillai as in 2 Samuel 17:27.

en.B: These looked for their entry among those listed in the family records, but they were not found there, so they were barred from the priesthood as unclean.
en.R: They looked for their names in the family records, but the names were not there. So they were not allowed to serve as priests, because they were treated as unclean.

es.L: Estos buscaron su registro [entre] los inscritos por genealogía, pero no se hallaron, y fueron tenidos por impuros [y excluidos] del sacerdocio.
es.B: Estos buscaron su inscripción en los registros de familias, pero no la encontraron, así que fueron excluidos del sacerdocio como impuros.
es.R: Buscaron sus nombres en los registros de familias, pero no estaban. Por eso no se les permitió servir como sacerdotes, porque los consideraron impuros.

fr.L: Ceux-ci cherchèrent leur registre [parmi] ceux qui étaient inscrits par généalogie, mais ils ne furent pas trouvés, et ils furent déclarés impurs [et exclus] du sacerdoce.
fr.B: Ils cherchèrent leur inscription dans les registres généalogiques, mais on ne l’y trouva pas ; ils furent donc écartés du sacerdoce comme impurs.
fr.R: Ils ont cherché leurs noms dans les registres des familles, mais leurs noms n’y étaient pas. Alors on ne les a pas laissés servir comme prêtres, parce qu’on les considérait comme impurs.

sw.L: Hawa walitafuta maandiko yao [kati ya] walioandikwa kwa nasaba, lakini hawakuonekana, wakahesabiwa kuwa najisi [na kuondolewa] katika ukuhani.
sw.B: Hawa walitafuta majina yao kati ya walioandikwa katika orodha za ukoo, lakini hayakupatikana humo, kwa hiyo wakazuiwa kuwa makuhani kwa kuwa walihesabiwa kuwa najisi.
sw.R: Walitafuta majina yao katika kumbukumbu za jamaa, lakini majina hayakuwamo. Kwa hiyo hawakuruhusiwa kutumika kama makuhani, kwa sababu walihesabiwa kuwa najisi.

vi.L: Những người này tìm sổ ghi của mình [trong số] những người được ghi vào gia phả, nhưng không tìm thấy, và họ bị coi là ô uế [và bị loại] khỏi chức tế lễ.
vi.B: Những người này tìm tên mình trong sổ gia phả nhưng không thấy, nên họ bị coi là ô uế và bị loại khỏi chức tế lễ.
vi.R: Họ tìm tên mình trong sổ ghi chép các gia đình, nhưng không có. Vì vậy họ không được phục vụ làm thầy tế lễ, vì bị coi là không tinh sạch.

decisions.choice: those enrolled by genealogy: the family registers
decisions.reason: Israel kept written records of families by descent (1 Chronicles 5:17; 9:1; Nehemiah 7:5). A priest had to show that he was descended from Aaron (Numbers 3:10; 17:5).

decisions.choice: defiled from the priesthood: declared unfit and kept out of the priesthood
decisions.reason: The verb means to be made unclean. With "from" it means they were treated as unclean and so excluded from the priests' service. The decision could be changed (verse 63).

decisions.choice: "walioandikwa kwa nasaba" (L), "orodha za ukoo" (B), "kumbukumbu za jamaa" (R)
decisions.reason: The family registers, in the wording the 1 Chronicles drafts use for genealogical enrollment.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַתִּרְשָׁ֨תָא֙ לָהֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יֹאכְל֖וּ מִקֹּ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֑ים עַ֛ד עֲמֹ֥ד כֹּהֵ֖ן לְאוּרִ֥ים וּלְתֻמִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the Tirshatha to them that not they should eat from [the] holy of the holy things until [there] stands a priest for Urim and for Thummim.

en.L: And the Tirshatha said to them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest stood up for Urim and Thummim.
en.B: The governor told them not to eat any of the most holy food until there was a priest to consult the Urim and Thummim.
en.R: The governor told them they must not eat the most holy food that belonged to the priests. They had to wait until there was a priest who could find out God's answer by using the Urim and Thummim.

es.L: Y el Tirsata les dijo que no comieran de las cosas santísimas hasta que se levantara un sacerdote para [consultar] el urim y el tumim.
es.B: El gobernador les dijo que no comieran de los alimentos santísimos hasta que hubiera un sacerdote que consultara el urim y el tumim.
es.R: El gobernador les dijo que no podían comer de los alimentos santísimos que les tocaban a los sacerdotes. Tenían que esperar hasta que hubiera un sacerdote que pudiera conocer la respuesta de Dios usando el urim y el tumim.

fr.L: Et le Tirshatha leur dit qu’ils ne mangeraient pas des choses très saintes jusqu’à ce qu’un prêtre se lève pour les ourim et les toummim.
fr.B: Le gouverneur leur dit de ne manger d’aucun des aliments très saints jusqu’à ce qu’il y ait un prêtre pour consulter les ourim et les toummim.
fr.R: Le gouverneur leur a dit qu’ils ne devaient pas manger la nourriture très sainte réservée aux prêtres. Ils devaient attendre qu’il y ait un prêtre capable de connaître la réponse de Dieu au moyen des ourim et des toummim.

sw.L: Naye Tirshatha akawaambia kwamba wasile katika vitu vitakatifu kuliko vyote mpaka kuhani asimame kwa ajili ya Urimu na Thumimu.
sw.B: Liwali akawaambia wasile chakula chochote kilicho kitakatifu kuliko vyote mpaka atakapokuwepo kuhani wa kuuliza kwa Urimu na Thumimu.
sw.R: Liwali aliwaambia wasile chakula kitakatifu sana kilichokuwa cha makuhani. Walipaswa kungoja mpaka atakapokuwepo kuhani ambaye angeweza kupata jibu la Mungu kwa kutumia Urimu na Thumimu.

vi.L: Và quan Tiệt-sa-tha bảo họ rằng họ không được ăn các vật chí thánh cho đến khi có một thầy tế lễ đứng lên [dùng] U-rim và Thu-mim.
vi.B: Quan tổng đốc bảo họ không được ăn các thức ăn chí thánh cho đến khi có một thầy tế lễ cầu hỏi bằng U-rim và Thu-mim.
vi.R: Quan tổng đốc bảo họ không được ăn thức ăn rất thánh dành cho các thầy tế lễ. Họ phải chờ đến khi có một thầy tế lễ có thể dùng U-rim và Thu-mim để biết câu trả lời của Đức Chúa Trời.

decisions.choice: the Tirshatha: a Persian title for the governor
decisions.reason: The word is a Persian title, probably meaning something like "his excellency". It is used of Nehemiah, the governor (Nehemiah 8:9; 10:2). Here it probably refers to Sheshbazzar or Zerubbabel, who led the return (1:8; 2:2; 5:14).

decisions.choice: the most holy things: the parts of the offerings that only priests could eat
decisions.reason: Certain parts of the grain offerings, sin offerings and guilt offerings were "most holy" and could be eaten only by priests (Leviticus 2:3; 6:10, 18, 22; 7:6; Numbers 18:9-10). Excluding these men from them meant not counting them as priests.

decisions.choice: the Urim and Thummim: the lots kept by the high priest
decisions.reason: The Urim and Thummim were kept in the high priest's breastpiece and used to receive the LORD's answer in hard cases (Exodus 28:30; Numbers 27:21; 1 Samuel 28:6). The text implies they were not in use at this time; the question was left until a priest could consult them. What they looked like and how they were used is not known.

decisions.choice: the Tirshatha (Literal), the governor (Balanced, Readable); Urim and Thummim at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Persian title as a name; Balanced and Readable say what it means. Urim and Thummim have no English equivalent and stay as names; Readable says what they were used for.

decisions.choice: "el Tirsata" (L); "el gobernador" (B, R); "el urim y el tumim"
decisions.reason: The terms note's choice for the Persian title; urim and tumim as the published Spanish of Exodus 28:30, lowercase.

decisions.choice: "Tirshatha" (L), "liwali" (B, R); "Urimu na Thumimu" at every level
decisions.reason: As the terms note: Literal keeps the Persian title as a name; "liwali" is the governor of 2 Kings 18:24. Urim and Thummim keep the Swahili Pentateuch forms.

decisions.choice: "le Tirshatha" (Literal); "le gouverneur" (Balanced, Readable); "les ourim et les toummim" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as the terms note: Literal keeps the Persian title as a name, Balanced and Readable say what it means. The lots keep the lowercase French form of Exodus 28:30.

decisions.choice: quan Tiệt-sa-tha (Literal); quan tổng đốc (Balanced, Readable); U-rim và Thu-mim
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Persian title as a name, as the English does; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the terms note gives. "U-rim" is the form of 1 Samuel 28:6, and "Thu-mim" is spelled to match.

decisions.choice: 42,360: more than the sum of the families listed
decisions.reason: The numbers in verses 3-60 add up to 29,818 (in Nehemiah 7 to 31,089), yet both lists give the same total, 42,360 (Nehemiah 7:66). The total may include people not listed by family, such as women and children, or members of other tribes; or numbers in the lists may have changed in copying, which happens easily with numbers. The text does not say.

decisions.choice: as one: all together, in total
decisions.reason: The phrase means the whole number counted together (Nehemiah 7:66; compare Ezra 3:1).

decisions.choice: male and female slaves: servants the families owned
decisions.reason: These were servants who belonged to the households, counted apart from the assembly. That there were one for every six people shows that some families had wealth.

decisions.choice: male and female singers: singers of the households, not the temple singers
decisions.reason: These are not the Levite singers of verse 41, who were men. They were probably singers for feasts and for mourning (2 Samuel 19:36; 2 Chronicles 35:25; Ecclesiastes 2:8). Nehemiah 7:67 has 245.

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal); servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's rule for this word: "slave" at Literal, "servant" at Balanced and Readable, with the meaning decision saying that they were owned.

decisions.choice: "esclavos y esclavas" (L); "siervos y siervas" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same rule as verse 55; the meaning decision says they were owned by the households.

decisions.choice: "watumwa" (L), "watumishi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The project's rule for this word, as the English; the meaning decision says they were owned.

decisions.choice: tôi trai, tớ gái
alternatives: nô lệ nam, nô lệ nữ
decisions.reason: The household servants are "tôi trai, tớ gái" at every level: the Vietnamese pair names servants a family owned without the harsher "nô lệ". The English has "slaves" at Literal, but Vietnamese keeps "nô lệ" for slavery as an institution (Jeremiah 34).

decisions.choice: ca sĩ
decisions.reason: These household singers are not the Levite singers of verse 41 (m2), so Balanced and Readable call them "ca sĩ" and keep "người ca hát" for the temple singers.

decisions.choice: horses and mules: missing from most Hebrew copies of Nehemiah 7
decisions.reason: In most Hebrew manuscripts Nehemiah 7 has no line for the horses and mules; translations that add it there number it Nehemiah 7:68. Horses and mules were for riding, so few families had them; camels and donkeys (verse 67) carried the loads.

decisions.reason: Donkeys were the ordinary animals for carrying loads and people. The journey from Babylon to Jerusalem took about four months (Ezra 7:9).

records.literal_gloss: And some of [the] heads of the fathers, in their coming to [the] house of the LORD which [is] in Jerusalem, offered freely for [the] house of God, to set it up on its place.

en.L: And some of the heads of the fathers, when they came to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} which [is] in Jerusalem, offered freely for the house of God, to set it up on its place.
en.B: Some of the heads of families, on coming to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem, made freewill offerings for the house of God, so that it could be set up again where it had stood.
en.R: When they reached the place in Jerusalem where the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had stood, some of the family leaders gave gifts freely so that God's temple could be built again in the same place.

es.L: Y algunos de los jefes de las [casas] paternas, cuando llegaron a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que [está] en Jerusalén, ofrecieron voluntariamente para la casa de Dios, para levantarla en su lugar.
es.B: Algunos de los jefes de familia, al llegar a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en Jerusalén, dieron ofrendas voluntarias para la casa de Dios, para que fuera levantada de nuevo donde había estado.
es.R: Cuando llegaron al lugar de Jerusalén donde había estado el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, algunos de los jefes de familia dieron ofrendas de buena voluntad para que el templo de Dios se construyera de nuevo en el mismo lugar.

fr.L: Et certains des chefs des pères, lorsqu’ils arrivèrent à la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} qui [est] à Jérusalem, firent des offrandes volontaires pour la maison de Dieu, afin de la relever à sa place.
fr.B: Quelques-uns des chefs des familles, en arrivant à la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} à Jérusalem, firent des offrandes volontaires pour la maison de Dieu, afin qu’elle soit rebâtie là où elle se trouvait.
fr.R: Quand ils sont arrivés à l’endroit de Jérusalem où se trouvait le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, certains chefs de famille ont donné librement des offrandes pour que le temple de Dieu soit reconstruit au même endroit.

sw.L: Na baadhi ya wakuu wa baba, walipofika kwenye nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} iliyoko Yerusalemu, wakatoa kwa hiari kwa ajili ya nyumba ya Mungu, ili kuisimamisha mahali pake.
sw.B: Baadhi ya wakuu wa jamaa, walipofika kwenye nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} iliyoko Yerusalemu, walitoa sadaka za hiari kwa ajili ya nyumba ya Mungu, ili ijengwe tena mahali ilipokuwa.
sw.R: Walipofika mahali huko Yerusalemu ambapo hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilikuwa limesimama, baadhi ya viongozi wa jamaa walitoa zawadi kwa hiari ili hekalu la Mungu lijengwe tena mahali pale pale.

vi.L: Và một số người đứng đầu các gia tộc, khi họ đến nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tại Giê-ru-sa-lem, đã dâng cách tự nguyện cho nhà của Đức Chúa Trời, để dựng nó lên tại chỗ cũ của nó.
vi.B: Một số trưởng tộc, khi đến nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tại Giê-ru-sa-lem, đã dâng lễ vật tự nguyện cho nhà của Đức Chúa Trời, để dựng lại nhà ấy tại chỗ cũ.
vi.R: Khi đến nơi đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tại Giê-ru-sa-lem trước kia đã đứng, một số người đứng đầu các gia đình tự nguyện dâng quà để đền thờ của Đức Chúa Trời được xây lại tại chính chỗ ấy.

decisions.choice: the house of the LORD: the temple site, still in ruins
decisions.reason: The Babylonians had burned the temple in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:9). The returning leaders came to the place where it had stood; the altar was set up first (3:2-3), then the foundation laid (3:10).

decisions.choice: to set it up on its place: to rebuild it on its old site
decisions.reason: The temple was to stand where the first one had stood, as the decree also says (5:15; 6:7).

decisions.choice: Readable says "the place ... where the temple had stood"
decisions.reason: The temple was a ruin when they arrived, so Readable makes clear that they came to its site.

source.text: כְּכֹחָ֗ם נָתְנוּ֮ לְאוֹצַ֣ר הַמְּלָאכָה֒ זָהָ֗ב דַּרְכְּמוֹנִים֙ שֵׁשׁ־רִבֹּ֣אות וָאֶ֔לֶףסוְכֶ֕סֶף מָנִ֖ים חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֑ים וְכָתְנֹ֥ת כֹּהֲנִ֖ים מֵאָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: According to their strength they gave to [the] treasury of the work: gold, darics six ten-thousands and a thousand, and silver, minas five thousand, and tunics of priests a hundred.

en.L: According to their ability they gave to the treasury of the work: gold, 61,000 darics, and silver, 5,000 minas, and 100 priests' tunics.
en.B: As they were able, they gave to the treasury for the work 61,000 darics of gold, {{units:about 3 tons|5,000 minas}} of silver and 100 garments for the priests.
en.R: Each family gave what it could afford for the work: 61,000 darics of gold, {{units:about 3 tons|5,000 minas}} of silver, and 100 sets of clothes for the priests.

es.L: Según sus fuerzas dieron al tesoro de la obra: oro, 61 000 dáricos, y plata, 5 000 minas, y 100 túnicas de sacerdotes.
es.B: Según sus posibilidades, dieron al tesoro para la obra 61 000 dáricos de oro, {{units:unas 3 toneladas|5 000 minas}} de plata y 100 vestiduras para los sacerdotes.
es.R: Cada familia dio lo que podía para la obra: 61 000 dáricos de oro, {{units:unas 3 toneladas|5 000 minas}} de plata y 100 juegos de ropa para los sacerdotes.

fr.L: Selon leurs moyens, ils donnèrent au trésor de l’ouvrage : en or, 61 000 dariques, et en argent, 5 000 mines, et 100 tuniques de prêtres.
fr.B: Selon leurs moyens, ils donnèrent au trésor de l’ouvrage 61 000 dariques d’or, {{units:environ 3 tonnes|5 000 mines}} d’argent et 100 vêtements pour les prêtres.
fr.R: Chaque famille a donné ce qu’elle pouvait pour les travaux : 61 000 dariques d’or, {{units:environ 3 tonnes|5 000 mines}} d’argent et 100 tenues pour les prêtres.

sw.L: Kwa kadiri ya uwezo wao walitoa kwa hazina ya kazi: dhahabu, darkoni 61,000, na fedha, mane 5,000, na kanzu za makuhani 100.
sw.B: Kwa kadiri walivyoweza, walitoa kwa hazina ya kazi darkoni 61,000 za dhahabu, {{units:karibu tani 3|mane 5,000}} za fedha na mavazi 100 ya makuhani.
sw.R: Kila jamaa ilitoa kwa kadiri ilivyoweza kwa ajili ya kazi: darkoni 61,000 za dhahabu, {{units:karibu tani 3|mane 5,000}} za fedha, na seti 100 za mavazi ya makuhani.

vi.L: Theo sức mình, họ dâng vào kho cho công việc: vàng, 61.000 đa-riếc, và bạc, 5.000 mi-na, và 100 áo dài của thầy tế lễ.
vi.B: Tùy theo khả năng, họ dâng vào kho cho công việc 61.000 đa-riếc vàng, {{units:khoảng 2.900 kg|5.000 mi-na}} bạc và 100 bộ áo cho các thầy tế lễ.
vi.R: Mỗi gia đình dâng tùy theo sức mình cho công việc: 61.000 đa-riếc vàng, {{units:khoảng 2,9 tấn|5.000 mi-na}} bạc, và 100 bộ áo cho các thầy tế lễ.

decisions.choice: darics: Persian gold coins
decisions.reason: The daric was the gold coin of the Persian empire, first struck under Darius I (522-486 BC), weighing a little over a quarter of an ounce. The writer counts the gift in the coin of his own day. The word could also stand for the Greek drachma.

decisions.choice: minas: a weight of silver
decisions.reason: A mina was fifty or sixty shekels (Ezekiel 45:12), about 1 1/4 pounds, so 5,000 minas weighed about 3 tons.

decisions.choice: Nehemiah 7:69-71 gives the gifts differently
decisions.reason: Nehemiah lists the gifts of the governor, of the heads of families and of the rest of the people: together 41,000 darics, 4,200 minas, 50 bowls and 597 priests' garments. The two accounts cannot be matched exactly.

decisions.choice: darics at every level; minas in a units span (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The daric is a coin, not a measure, so it keeps its name at every level. Literal keeps "minas"; Balanced and Readable give the modern weight with the mina as the alternative.

decisions.choice: "dáricos" at every level; minas in a units span (B, R)
decisions.reason: The daric is a coin, so it keeps its name at every level, as the terms note says; Literal keeps "minas", and Balanced and Readable give the weight at the Pentateuch value (0.6 kg a mina: 3 000 kg) with the mina as the alternative.

decisions.choice: "darkoni" at every level (1 Chronicles 29:7); minas in a units span, metric "karibu tani 3" with "mane 5,000" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The daric is a coin and keeps its name; as the Swahili style guide, the units setting defaults to metric, unlike the English pounds.

decisions.choice: "dariques" at every level; "environ 3 tonnes" with "5 000 mines" as the alternative
decisions.reason: For the whole book: French gives metric weights by default (a mina about 0.6 kg, as Kings and the Pentateuch), where the English gives pounds and tons. The daric is a coin, not a weight, so it keeps its name at every level, as the English does.

decisions.choice: đa-riếc at every level; mi-na in a units span (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The daric is a coin, so "đa-riếc" (the form of 1 Chronicles 29:7) is kept at every level and not converted. Literal keeps "mi-na"; Balanced and Readable give the metric weight by default (a mina about 0.57 kg, so 5,000 minas about 2.9 tonnes), with the mina as the alternative. The English converts to US units.

source.text: וַיֵּשְׁב֣וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְ֠הַלְוִיִּם וּֽמִן־הָעָ֞ם וְהַמְשֹׁרְרִ֧ים וְהַשּׁוֹעֲרִ֛ים וְהַנְּתִינִ֖ים בְּעָרֵיהֶ֑ם וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּעָרֵיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And dwelt the priests and the Levites and some of the people and the singers and the gatekeepers and the Nethinim in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.

en.L: And the priests and the Levites and some of the people and the singers and the gatekeepers and the Nethinim lived in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.
en.B: So the priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers and the temple servants lived in their towns, and all Israel lived in their towns.
en.R: So the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the temple servants and some of the people settled in their own towns. All the other Israelites settled in their towns too.

es.L: Y los sacerdotes y los levitas y [algunos] del pueblo y los cantores y los porteros y los netineos habitaron en sus ciudades, y todo Israel en sus ciudades.
es.B: Así, los sacerdotes, los levitas, parte del pueblo, los cantores, los porteros y los servidores del templo se establecieron en sus ciudades, y todo Israel vivió en sus ciudades.
es.R: Así, los sacerdotes, los levitas, los cantores, los porteros, los servidores del templo y parte del pueblo se establecieron en sus propias ciudades. Todos los demás israelitas también se establecieron en sus ciudades.

fr.L: Et les prêtres et les Lévites et une partie du peuple et les chanteurs et les portiers et les Nethinim habitèrent dans leurs villes, et tout Israël dans leurs villes.
fr.B: Ainsi les prêtres, les Lévites, une partie du peuple, les chanteurs, les portiers et les serviteurs du temple s’établirent dans leurs villes, et tout Israël s’établit dans ses villes.
fr.R: Ainsi les prêtres, les Lévites, les chanteurs, les portiers, les serviteurs du temple et une partie du peuple se sont installés dans leurs villes. Tous les autres Israélites se sont aussi installés dans leurs villes.

sw.L: Na makuhani na Walawi na baadhi ya watu na waimbaji na mabawabu na Wanethinimu wakakaa katika miji yao, na Israeli wote katika miji yao.
sw.B: Hivyo makuhani, Walawi, baadhi ya watu, waimbaji, mabawabu na watumishi wa hekalu walikaa katika miji yao, na Israeli wote wakakaa katika miji yao.
sw.R: Hivyo makuhani, Walawi, waimbaji, walinzi wa malango, watumishi wa hekalu na baadhi ya watu walikaa katika miji yao wenyewe. Waisraeli wengine wote nao wakakaa katika miji yao.

vi.L: Và các thầy tế lễ, người Lê-vi, một số dân chúng, những người ca hát, những người giữ cổng và người Nê-thi-nim ở trong các thành của họ, và cả Y-sơ-ra-ên ở trong các thành của họ.
vi.B: Vậy các thầy tế lễ, người Lê-vi, một số dân chúng, những người ca hát, những người giữ cổng và những người phục dịch đền thờ sống trong các thành của mình, và cả Y-sơ-ra-ên sống trong các thành của mình.
vi.R: Vậy các thầy tế lễ, người Lê-vi, những người ca hát, những người giữ cổng, những người phục dịch đền thờ và một số dân chúng định cư trong các thành của mình. Tất cả những người Y-sơ-ra-ên khác cũng định cư trong các thành của họ.

decisions.choice: some of the people: perhaps those who lived in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As it stands the verse names "some of the people" without saying where they lived. The Greek book of 1 Esdras, which retells this chapter, says that some lived in Jerusalem and the country around it, which may preserve words lost here; Nehemiah 11:1 says that later only a tenth of the people lived in Jerusalem. The Hebrew is translated as it stands.

decisions.choice: all Israel: the returned community as the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Though most of them were from Judah and Benjamin, the book calls the returned community Israel (3:1; 6:17, where they offer twelve goats "for all Israel").

decisions.choice: Readable says "all the other Israelites" and "too"
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the second group is everyone not already named.
